article.title: Coalition to Protest Lynn Fitch’s Decision in Police Killing of Baby Kohen Wiley
article.author: Sharon Kyle
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Press Release Black Lives Matter Grassroots, Building Bridges Coalition, Movement for Black Lives, Jackson People’s Assembly, and a host of community groups are planning to protest Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch to unequivocally denounce her determination that the murder of baby Kohen Wiley was “justified.” Senatobia police Sergeant Hunter Foster. Foster, who has a documented history of racism and violence, shot the one-year-old dead in his mother’s arms on June 14, 2026. This is one of the most egregious and horrifying acts of anti-Black violence that we have seen from police anywhere. Police should have never been called. Sergeant Foster should never have fired his weapon. And the murder can never be justified. We have had enough of white supremacist systems terrorizing our communities and stealing Black lives, with no liability or consequence.. Foster resigned from the Senatobia police department last week in light of leaked video footage that shows him shooting into the passenger side of the vehicle where Baby Kohen was being held by his mother. Murderous cop Hunter Foster shot into the car - striking the friend and killing Baby Kohen. Foster was clearly out of the path of the vehicle that he pursued on foot. Neither the mother or her friend were suspected of any crime. “What kind of world is this when the murder of a baby could ever be deemed ‘justified’? Senatobia police, Lynn Fitch, and Walmart all have blood on their hands and there must be consequences. They don’t get to murder our babies with impunity,” says Dr. Melina Abdullah of Black Lives Matter Grassroots. We condemn Walmart for calling police on a Black mother. We condemn killer cop Hunter Foster for shooting a precious Black baby. We condemn the Senatobia Police Department for serving as a breeding ground for racist violence and greenlighting the killing and terrorization of Black people. We condemn Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch for giving the green light to police to kill - even babies - with absolute impunity. Memorials for Baby Kohen have already restarted. November 1st marks what should have been Baby Kohen’s second birthday. Black Lives Matter Grassroots and Building Bridges Coalition are planning a weekend of events in collaboration with Baby Kohen’s family in both Senatobia and Jackson, Mississippi. These activations are meant to memorialize his short life, support community healing and empowerment, and rally for justice in Kohen’s name. “Kohen’s entire family is in unimaginable pain. They should be celebrating his birthday, not mourning his death. The community is organizing and demanding accountability,” says Marquell Bridges, of the Building Bridges Coalition, who has been organizing alongside Kohen’s family since the killing. In addition, from October 30th through November 2nd, Baby Kohen’s family, Black Lives Matter Grassroots and the Building Bridges Coalition is calling for community to: Boycott Walmart. Demand the firing of killer cop Hunter Foster. Oppose Attorney General Lynn Fitch, especially in her bid for Mississippi Governor. Pluginwith @blmgrassroots on Instagram for next steps. Justice in the name of Baby Kohen Wiley!
